Hi Vanessa,

We're finalizing the SOW and procurement packet for Redwood's Hosted API and legal asked for a short, customer-facing one-pager (and a 2-3 sentence snippet we can publish in procurement docs) that answers the usual questions:

- Which subprocessors handle request content and where are they located?
- Do you use SCCs / other transfer mechanisms for cross-border processing?
- What parts of requests/outputs are stored and for how long (retention)?
- Key management options (bring-your-own-key / KMS integrations) and whether Redwood can access keys
- Any data residency / regional routing controls for hosted customers

Can you share a publishable snippet and a brief one-pager we can attach to the SOW? We need this for our procurement review and to include with our vendor risk questionnaire. Ideally something concise and plain-language, not full legalese.

Target timeline: procurement meeting on Tuesday (2028-06-13), so if possible by EOD Monday (2028-06-12).

Thanks — happy to hop on a 15 if it's easier.

—Maria

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>

Date: 2028-06-11T14:27:00Z
Subject: Draft language for Acme — publishable snippet + one-pager notes

Vanessa / Laura — first pass below. Kept it concise and procurement-friendly; flagged a couple of legal notes that should not go into the public snippet but are fine in the one-pager.

PUBLISHABLE SNIPPET (2–3 sentences; copy Acme can include in vendor packet):
"Redwood Inference processes Hosted API requests using subprocessors for compute and storage. We maintain a public subprocessors list and use EU Standard Contractual Clauses (or equivalent mechanisms) for cross-border transfers. Customers can request data residency controls and integrate with customer-managed KMS keys for encryption at rest; Redwood does not have access to customer-managed KMS keys unless explicitly configured. Request content and generated outputs are retained per customer-configured retention settings; default transit logs are kept for 30 days for troubleshooting and abuse prevention."

ONE-PAGER OUTLINE / NOTES (for Laura to format):
- Intro: scope (Hosted API only) and applicability (customer-managed vs hosted tiers).
- Subprocessors: short table (role: compute / storage / monitoring), example vendors, and region locations. Link to public subprocessor list.
- Data flows: stepwise mapping (ingest -> transient compute -> optional persistent storage -> logs/metrics). Clarify that model inference is stateless by default; persistent storage only used if customer enables fine-tuning or request/response logging.
- Transfers & safeguards: SCCs in place; list fallback mechanisms (e.g., EU-region hosting, contractual addenda). Note: include link to transfer impact assessment.
- Retention & deletion: default retention windows and how to request deletion or shorter retention.
- KMS & key management: BYOK options and tech caveat — if BYOK is enabled, Redwood cannot decrypt without customer permission; we store key references only.
- Legal caveats (internal only): avoid categorical phrases like "we never access data"; accuracy around model outputs and recording of some telemetry. Also include how we handle lawful requests / subpoenas and customer notification timelines per contract.

Attachments to include in the one-pager package: hosted-data-transfer-onepager-v1.pdf (clean PDF for procurement), publishable-privacy-snippet.txt (exact copy for procurement docs), and a link to the live subprocessor registry.

Questions for Vanessa: any vendor names you want redacted or replaced with "subprocessor partners" for Acme? Also confirm whether Acme will require a signed Data Processing Addendum (DPA) with specific subprocessor disclosure timing — that will change whether we send a static CSV or provide a live link.

—Kimberly
Kimberly Park
